draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kanchipuram! They call it the City of Thousand Temples, full of huge temple towers and 1000-pillared halls. And yes, this is where the famous Kanjeevaram silk saris come from.
draft.hungryLine: Between temples, look for a simple local spot for a hot South Indian meal, and ask around for what the town is cooking today.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Start with the Kailasanathar Temple and the Vaikunta Perumal Temple, two of the city's big historic monuments.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Wander the silk shops and watch the saris come out, it's a slower, cooler break from temple hopping.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The name comes from kanchi and puram, meaning the city of kanchi flowers, because those flowers grew all over here.

tips.title: Dress for temples.
tips.body: This is a city of temples, so keep shoulders and knees covered and be ready to leave your shoes outside.

tips.title: Shop for silk here.
tips.body: Kanchipuram is famous for its silk saris, so this is the place to pick one up.

story.title: City of kanchi flowers
story.body: Kanchipuram grew up on the banks of the Vegavathy and Palar rivers. Its name means the city of kanchi flowers, which grew in plenty here.

story.title: A Pallava city
story.body: The Pallavas ruled here and the city became famous for its temple building. The Kailasanathar and Vaikunta Perumal temples are among its great monuments.

story.title: Many dynasties
story.body: After the Pallavas came the Medieval and Later Cholas, the Later Pandyas, the Vijayanagara Empire and the Carnatic kingdom.

story.title: Conjeeveram
story.body: The British ruled the city too and called it Conjeeveram. It also went by Kanjeevaram, the name the silk saris still carry.

story.title: Temples and silk
story.body: Kanchipuram is the capital of its district and part of the Chennai metropolitan area. It draws visitors from India and abroad for its temples and saris.
